summary: Describes five kinds of SNMP applications that use an SNMP engine: command generators, command responders, notification originators, notification receivers and proxy forwarders. It also defines MIB modules for specifying targets of management operations, filtering notifications and configuring proxy forwarding.

eli5.summary: Network managers do different jobs: ask questions, answer them, shout about problems, listen for shouts, and pass messages along. This note names those five jobs and how each one works.

questions: what is an snmp command responder
what is an snmp proxy forwarder
subtitle: The five jobs an SNMP program can do, how each one behaves, and the MIB tables that say where notifications go.

tldr.problem: An SNMP engine only handles messages. Something has to sit on top of it to ask questions, answer them, send alerts, receive alerts and relay messages, and each of those jobs needs clear rules.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3413 defines five application types (command generators, command responders, notification originators, notification receivers and proxy forwarders) with step-by-step procedures for each, plus three MIB modules that configure targets, notification filtering and proxy forwarding.
tldr.outcome: It is an Internet Standard (STD 62) and replaced RFC 2573. Its target, notification and proxy MIB modules are the standard way to make this behavior configurable over SNMP.

today: RFC 3413 is an Internet Standard (STD 62) and obsoletes RFC 2573. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Five Kinds of SNMP Application
sections.content:
RFC 3413 describes five types of application that make use of an SNMP engine as described in RFC 3411. A command generator starts Read-Class and Write-Class requests and handles the responses. A command responder receives those requests, performs them under access control and sends back a response.

A notification originator watches for events and generates Notification-Class messages. A notification receiver listens for them and answers when a message carries a Confirmed-Class PDU. A proxy forwarder passes SNMP messages along.

There is no restriction on which types are attached to one engine. A single engine may serve both a command generator and a command responder. Proxy forwarding is optional, and the sections about proxies may be skipped by implementations that do not include one.
sections.eli5: Think of a school office with five jobs: someone who asks questions, someone who answers, someone who rings the alarm, someone who listens for the alarm, and a messenger who carries notes between rooms. One person can do more than one job.

sections.title: Management Targets
sections.content:
Notification originators and proxy forwarders need to know where and how to send a message. RFC 3413 calls that information a management target. It has two parts: destination information (a transport domain and a transport address, together called a transport endpoint) and SNMP parameters (message processing model, security model, security level and security name).

The SNMP-TARGET-MIB module holds one table for each kind of information. The relationship is many-to-many: several endpoints can share one set of SNMP parameters, and one endpoint can be used with several sets of parameters.

Entries in the address table carry a tag list, a way to group them. A tag is an arbitrary string of octets that must not contain a space, TAB, carriage return or line feed, and it cannot be zero length inside a list. A list has no leading, trailing or doubled delimiters.
sections.eli5: A management target is like an address book entry plus a note on how to write the letter: where it goes, and which secret handshake to use. Tags are sticky labels so you can say 'send this to everyone labeled group1'.

sections.title: Command Generators and Responders
sections.content:
A command generator calls the Dispatcher with sendPdu, giving the transport domain and address, message processing model, security model, security name, security level, context engine ID, context name, PDU version, the PDU and whether a response is expected. It should store the returned sendPduHandle to match a response to its request. A response is discarded if the message processing model, security model, security name, context engine ID, context name or PDU version differ from the original request, or if the request-id differs.

A command responder first calls registerContextEngineID for the PDU types it handles. If another responder already holds that registration, further attempts are denied, and in practice only a single command responder should be registered with an engine. When a request arrives through processPdu, the responder performs the operation against the relevant MIB view, calling isAccessAllowed to check each object instance.

Access failures map to protocol errors. A noSuchView, noAccessEntry or noGroupName result yields an authorizationError with error-index 0. An otherError yields genError with the index of the failed variable binding. A noSuchContext result increments the snmpUnknownContexts counter, and a known but unavailable context increments snmpUnavailableContexts; in both cases no result PDU is generated and a report is produced. A responder should always call returnResponsePdu, even after an error such as a resource allocation failure.
sections.eli5: The asker writes a question on a card and keeps a ticket number. When an answer comes back it checks the ticket matches. The answerer first checks the rulebook to see whether the asker may know that, and says 'not allowed' if not.

sections.title: Notifications: Sending and Receiving
sections.content:
A notification originator decides which context the information lives in, which management targets should hear about it, which PDU type each target gets and, for Confirmed-Class PDUs, the retry count and retransmission algorithm. Then, for each target, it filters, checks access, builds the PDU and sends it.

The per-target steps are: apply any filtering; fetch the variable bindings from within the relevant MIB view using isAccessAllowed with a notify view; check the notification type OID (the value of snmpTrapOID.0, the second variable binding) the same way; build a PDU with a locally unique request-id and error-status and error-index of 0; then call sendPdu. If the PDU is Unconfirmed-Class, no response is expected. If it is Confirmed-Class, the originator caches the target information and resends until a response arrives or the retry count is exceeded. Some report indications count as failure and need not be retried.

A notification receiver registers with a wildcard context engine ID and the PDU types it wants. For an Unconfirmed-Class PDU it extracts the fields and what happens next depends on the implementation. For a Confirmed-Class PDU it builds a Response-Class PDU with the same request-id and variable bindings, error-status and error-index 0, and returns it with returnResponsePdu.
sections.eli5: The alarm ringer checks who is allowed to hear which alarm, then rings it. For a 'please confirm' alarm it keeps ringing a few times until someone says 'got it'. The listener just says 'got it' with the same ticket number.

sections.title: Proxy Forwarders
sections.content:
RFC 3413 uses the word proxy in a deliberately narrow way: a proxy forwarder forwards SNMP messages to other engines according to the context, without regard to which managed object types they contain. A traditional agent's command responder, which processes requests by the names of individual objects, is not a proxy forwarder in this sense. A design goal is to act as an intermediary: for a forwarded Confirmed Notification-Class message, the response is forwarded when it arrives from the target rather than generated immediately.

For a request, the forwarder registers each context engine ID and PDU type it forwards (never its own engine's ID). It translates the incoming target information into one outgoing target, builds a new PDU with a unique request-id, sends it, and caches the sendPduHandle, original request-id, context, state reference and both target descriptions. If no outgoing target is found, or the cache cannot be written, it increments snmpProxyDrops and returns an error. When the response comes back it matches the cache, restores the original request-id and returns the response. Internal-Class PDUs such as Report PDUs are returned the same way, unless the original SNMP version cannot carry Report PDUs.

For a notification the translation may give several outgoing targets. The forwarder re-sends using the originator procedure, with the original context, no filtering and no access control on the variable bindings. For a Confirmed-Class original, it answers once at least one forwarded notification is acknowledged.
sections.eli5: A proxy is a mail clerk who does not read your letters. He only looks at the address, passes the letter to the next office, and hands the reply back to you.

sections.title: The Three MIB Modules
sections.content:
The SNMP-TARGET-MIB has the snmpTargetAddrTable (transport domain, address, timeout, retry count, tag list and a pointer to parameters) and the snmpTargetParamsTable (message processing model, security model, security name and security level). The default timeout is 1500 and the default retry count is 3, within a range of 0 to 255.

The SNMP-NOTIFICATION-MIB has the snmpNotifyTable, where each active entry selects address-table rows whose tag list contains the entry's snmpNotifyTag, and an snmpNotifyType of trap(1) or inform(2) that picks Unconfirmed-Class or Confirmed-Class PDUs. One address entry can be selected by several notify entries, so both traps and informs can go to the same target. It also holds the filter profile and filter tables.

For filtering, a notification name must be specifically included, and none of its object instances may be specifically excluded. Among matching filter entries, the one whose subtree has the most sub-identifiers decides, and a mask bit of zero acts as a wild card.

The SNMP-PROXY-MIB has the snmpProxyTable. For a request, it picks the matching row with the lexicographically smallest snmpProxyName, checking proxy type, context engine ID, context name (if supported) and the incoming parameters entry. Its snmpProxySingleTargetOut names one outgoing address. For notifications it selects all matching rows, and snmpProxyMultipleTargetOut is a tag that selects a set of address entries.
sections.eli5: The three MIBs are three forms an administrator fills in: one lists where messages can go, one says which alarms go to which list and which to hide, and one tells the mail clerk where to forward each kind of letter.

sections.title: Security and the Trap Example
sections.content:
These applications typically have direct access to MIB instrumentation, so the RFC says it is very important that they be strict in applying access control. A notification generator that gets its information by other means, such as from a command line, must not reveal information that access control would normally hide. The MIBs themselves hold potentially sensitive information, so a security administrator may wish to limit access to them.

Appendix A configures a notification generator to send traps to three managers: two with authentication and no privacy under the name joe, in the tag group group1, and one with authentication and privacy under the name bob, in group2. All three use UDP port 162.
sections.eli5: The helpers can reach private information, so they must follow the rules about who may see what. The example shows one alarm list that uses a plain lock and another that uses a lock plus a secret code.
